name.text: Choosing a method to estimate an area

questiontext.text:
For each situation, choose the method that fits the information given.

(a) {@s1@}

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

(b) {@s2@}

[[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]]

(c) {@s3@}

[[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]]

(d) {@s4@}

[[input:ans4]] [[validation:ans4]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Counting squares needs only an outline; the trapezoidal rule needs heights at the edges of the strips; the mid-ordinate rule needs heights at the middles.

(a) [[if test="is(mr[1]=\"C\")"]]counting squares: there is only an outline on a grid, with no measurements.[[elif test="is(mr[1]=\"T\")"]]the trapezoidal rule: the measurements are at the edges of equal strips, including both ends.[[else]]the mid-ordinate rule: the measurements are at the middles of equal strips, with none at the edges.[[/if]]

(b) [[if test="is(mr[2]=\"C\")"]]counting squares: there is only an outline on a grid, with no measurements.[[elif test="is(mr[2]=\"T\")"]]the trapezoidal rule: the measurements are at the edges of equal strips, including both ends.[[else]]the mid-ordinate rule: the measurements are at the middles of equal strips, with none at the edges.[[/if]]

(c) [[if test="is(mr[3]=\"C\")"]]counting squares: there is only an outline on a grid, with no measurements.[[elif test="is(mr[3]=\"T\")"]]the trapezoidal rule: the measurements are at the edges of equal strips, including both ends.[[else]]the mid-ordinate rule: the measurements are at the middles of equal strips, with none at the edges.[[/if]]

(d) [[if test="is(mr[4]=\"C\")"]]counting squares: there is only an outline on a grid, with no measurements.[[elif test="is(mr[4]=\"T\")"]]the trapezoidal rule: the measurements are at the edges of equal strips, including both ends.[[else]]the mid-ordinate rule: the measurements are at the middles of equal strips, with none at the edges.[[/if]]

questiondescription.text:
Area Approximations: choosing a method to estimate an area

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.2 (d) / Essential 2.1 (d): Match each situation to counting squares, the trapezoidal rule or the mid-ordinate rule, from where the measurements were taken.

Core and Essential

This question is original to this project.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core and Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

(a) The area can be estimated. Ask what you have: a drawing on a grid, or measurements, and where the measurements were taken.

[[elif test="is(rc1=2)"]]

(a) Counting squares needs a drawing of the shape on a grid. Here there are measurements and no drawing.

[[elif test="is(rc1=3)"]]

(a) Both rules need heights or widths measured at equal steps. Here there is only a shape on a grid of squares.

[[elif test="is(rc1=4)"]]

(a) The trapezoidal rule needs a measurement at both edges of every strip, including the two ends. {@rd1@}
